## ⚡ Elite Saver Workflow — Operating Contract (READ FIRST, EVERY SESSION)

> You are running inside an "Elite Saver" Task-Loop session. This contract is binding and overrides default verbosity. Purpose: minimize token burn — **input *and* output** — while a single CLI session drives an entire backlog branch from checkout to merge.

### Macro / Micro Git Lifecycle

```
[ main ]  (stable baseline)
   |
   +--> checkout branch/backlog-1  -->  NEW Claude CLI session (Session 1)
   |                                        |
   |                                 +--------------------------------------+
   |                                 |          TASK EXECUTION LOOP          |
   |                                 |     (Task 1 .. 15, SAME session)      |
   |                                 +--------------------------------------+
   |                                        |
   |     -- MICRO CYCLE per task (skills, context cutting & TDD) ---------------
   |                                        |
   |   [0] SKILL GATE   ->  Superpowers if available:
   |                         feature=brainstorm/spec, bug=systematic-debugging,
   |                         non-trivial change=TDD, finish=verification
   |   [1] GIT DIFF     ->  live diff = the "epicenter" (exact changed lines)
   |   [2] GRAPHIFY     ->  MACRO: map impacted files            (if indexed)
   |   [3] CODEGRAPH    ->  MICRO: pull ONLY the symbol/function (if indexed)
   |   [4] PONYTAIL     ->  reuse existing code, stdlib/native first,
   |                         smallest safe diff, no speculative dependency
   |   [5] CAVEMAN      ->  terse communication, zero fluff, maximum signal
   |   [6] RTK (IN)     ->  squeeze whitespace + strip junk comments (terminal)
   |                                        |
   |   ================== INSTRUCTION GATE ==================
   |                                        |
   |   [7] CLAUDE/AGENTS->  CODE-ONLY RULE ......  OUTPUT LOCKED
   |                                        |
   |   ================== IMPLEMENTATION ====================
   |                                        |
   |   [8] TDD (RED)    ->  write failing test first, verify via rtk
   |   [9] TDD (GREEN)  ->  write minimal code to pass, verify via rtk
   |   [10] TDD (REFACTOR)-> refactor under green, keep fixtures identical
   |                                        |
   |   ==================== COMPLETION ======================
   |                                        |
   |   [11] VERIFY      ->  verification-before-completion or local equivalent
   |   [12] UPDATE DOCS ->  update CLAUDE.md + docs/ (final task)
   |   [13] PR UPDATE   ->  one backlog branch = one PR with task checklist
   |   [14] CI CHECK    ->  run `make test` + `go vet ./...` green (no self-hosted CI)
   |   [15] GIT MERGE   ->  merge verified PR & push to main
   |
   +-- PR merged to main  -->  CLOSE Session 1 (cache reset cleanly)
   |
   +--> checkout branch/backlog-2  -->  NEW Claude CLI session (Session 2) ... repeat
```

### Backlog / PR Contract
1. **1 Backlog = 1 branch = 1 PR.** A backlog prompt may contain many tasks, but they stay on the same backlog branch and the same PR unless the user explicitly asks to split.
2. **PR follows the prompt.** Use the backlog title and written task list as the PR title/body/checklist source of truth; do not invent scope beyond it.
3. **One task loop, one PR update stream.** Commit task-sized changes as needed, but update the same PR instead of opening one PR per task.
4. **No silent main-only implementation.** For implementation/backlog work, create or update the backlog PR before completion unless the user explicitly requests direct-to-main work.
5. **Mandatory Green Before Merge.** A PR MUST NOT be merged until `make test` (`go test -v -race ./...`) and `go vet ./...` pass 100% GREEN. Never declare work completed while tests are red or unverified.
6. **Strict Red-Repair Protocol.** If a test/vet run fails, the agent MUST immediately inspect the failure output, apply systematic fixes, commit, and re-verify until GREEN before completing the task or merging.
7. **Mandatory AgentMemory Post-Merge Retention.** Immediately after a PR merge to `main`, invoke `agentmemory` (`memory_save` / `remember` skill) to record implementation insights, architecture decisions, and PR summary so durable project memory is preserved across future sessions.
8. **Mandatory Docs Sync.** Code changes travel with docs: update `docs/CHANGELOG.md` (every merged change), the matching `docs/features/FEAT-*.md` spec, and phase report when behavior changes; `docs/` is the canonical history of the codebase. New failure modes get rows in `docs/operations/troubleshooting.md`.
9. **Security Preservation.** This is an auth/policy gateway. Never weaken: SHA-256 API key hashing, PolicyEngine precedence (`Global Deny > Per-Key Deny > Per-Key Allow`), header isolation on upstream 9Router calls, credential redaction (`json:"-"`), rate limiter semantics. Security review before any auth/policy change.

### Universal Harness Mandates (bind on EVERY harness)

> These mandates are **harness-agnostic** — they apply whether or not Superpowers/MCP tooling is mounted in the current runtime. Each names a primary tool AND its required fallback; when the tool is absent the fallback is mandatory, never a licence to skip the step.

**U1 — Superpowers-first implementation.** For any non-trivial implementation, drive the work through the Superpowers skill pipeline when available: `brainstorming`/`spec` to frame the change, `test-driven-development` to build it (RED → GREEN → REFACTOR), `systematic-debugging` for bugs, and `verification-before-completion` before declaring done. If Superpowers is not mounted, run the equivalent local workflow (write the failing test first, minimal green, refactor under green, then verify) — mention the fallback only if it changes the outcome. Never jump straight to production code on non-trivial work; a test or spec must precede it.

**U2 — Full-conversation retention after merge.** Immediately after a PR merges to `main` — in addition to the insight record required by §7 above — persist the **entire session** to `agentmemory` via `memory_save`: the user's requests and their verbatim intent, the decisions taken and *why*, the commands/commits/PRs involved, blockers hit and how they were fixed, and any open follow-ups. The goal is that a fresh session can resume with full context and nothing is lost when this window resets. If `agentmemory` is unavailable in the harness, write the same end-to-end digest to the file-based memory under `memory/` and add its `MEMORY.md` pointer line.

### Protocol IN — skill/context acquisition (cut INPUT tokens)
1. **You are in a Task Loop** — long-lived across many tasks. Never re-derive context already established in-session.
2. **Skill Gate before action.** If Superpowers skills are available, invoke the relevant one before reading/editing: brainstorming/spec for features, systematic-debugging for bugs, test-driven-development for non-trivial changes, and verification-before-completion before final status. If unavailable, follow the equivalent local workflow and mention the fallback only if it matters.
3. **Diff before read.** Begin each task from the live `git diff` (the epicenter). Never open a file blind.
4. **Graphify = blast radius (MACRO).** Map which files the diff impacts via `graphify` **before** reading any file in full, when the repo is indexed (`graphify-out/`).
5. **CodeGraph = surgical cut (MICRO).** Pull only the affected symbol via `codegraph_explore`. Do **not** read a whole file when a symbol suffices.
6. **Ponytail Check.** Before editing, choose the smallest safe fix: reuse existing code first, stdlib/native platform before dependencies, no speculative abstraction, no new dependency unless required.
7. **Caveman Mode.** Keep responses terse and fluff-free. Focus strictly on technical facts, diffs, and precise actions. Use `/caveman-compress` when updating context/docs.
8. **RTK at the terminal.** Route every shell / git / build / test through `rtk` (60–90% fewer tokens). Never run a raw chatty command when an `rtk` filter exists.

### Protocol TDD — test-first implementation (lock CORRECTNESS)
1. **Red before code.** Write the failing test first — one behaviour per test, named for the behaviour. No production line exists until a test demands it.
2. **Prove the red.** Run via `rtk go test` and confirm it fails for the *intended* reason — not an import/typo, **nor a crash-class failure** (panic / OOM / deadlock / timeout). A red that crashes the test runner is **NOT** a valid red — abort and fix the test fixture (mocks, isolation, stubs) before proceeding to green. Read the actual error message, not just the exit code. A test green on its first run proves nothing.
3. **Green minimal.** Write the least code that makes it pass — no untested branch, no speculative abstraction (diff-style, per Protocol OUT).
4. **Prove the green.** Re-run: the new test **and** the full suite pass before the next step. Never stack a fresh red on an unproven green.
5. **Refactor under green.** Clean only while green; re-run after each edit. Behaviour-preserving changes keep any golden/characterization fixtures **byte-identical** — regenerate only on an intentional contract change.
6. **Pin the contract.** The test stays as the next Micro Cycle's safety net, so its `git diff` (the IN epicenter) starts from a proven baseline. Docs travel with code.
7. **No completion without verification.** Before claiming done, run the smallest relevant verification and the Superpowers `verification-before-completion` skill when available; otherwise apply the same checklist locally.

### Protocol OUT — generation (lock OUTPUT tokens) — **CODE-ONLY + CAVEMAN**
1. **Caveman Brevity.** Respond terse like smart caveman (`caveman`). Drop articles (a/an/the), filler (just/really/basically), pleasantries, and hedging. Technical substance exact, fragments OK. Code unchanged.
2. **No pleasantries.** Zero greetings, intros, outros, recaps, congratulations, or "hope this helps." The reply *is* the artifact.
3. **Diff-style edits only.** Emit changed lines; for untouched regions use a cut-comment (`// ... unchanged ...`) instead of reprinting them.
4. **No process narration.** Don't preface ("I will now…") or summarize ("In summary…") unless explicitly asked.
5. **Prose is a last resort** — one tight line, never a paragraph.
6. **Safety overrides brevity (the only exception):** irreversible/destructive actions still get a one-line confirmation; genuine ambiguity still gets a question.
7. **Document on completion.** If the backlog or branch execution is completed on the final task, update `CLAUDE.md` and relevant modular docs under `docs/` according to the context of the branch worked on, then commit and push.
8. **Verification & merge.** Once `make test` and `go vet ./...` pass green on the branch, execute the merge into `main`.
